transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I was promoted to a supervisor role recently, but I'm really struggling because my mind keeps drifting off in meetings and calls. I get distracted so easily that it’s starting to seriously hurt my job performance, and I need to figure out why I'm having such a hard time staying mentally present.

Have you had problems with attention and distractibility since childhood or school, or did this mainly start recently after your promotion? Before this new role, were these focus problems present in other parts of your life too?

This actually goes all the way back to childhood; even in elementary school, my teachers always wrote that I daydreamed, forgot my homework, and couldn't sit still. It really turned into a major crisis after my promotion about 14 months ago, but it definitely affects my personal life too. Lately, I've been forgetting to pay bills on time and even forgetting to call my divorce lawyer back because my head is so scattered.

When your focus gets worse, is it mainly because your mind is tied up with constant worry and tension, or because you’ve been feeling down and losing interest in things? Or do the attention problems feel present even when you’re not especially anxious or depressed?

The attention problems are definitely there even when I'm not feeling anxious or down. While my divorce is stressful and makes things harder to manage, this is a lifelong pattern that started way before my current worries. My mind just naturally drifts off and I feel restless regardless of my mood.

Do these attention and restlessness problems happen in multiple settings, like at work, at home, and in social situations, or mainly just at work? Can you give one or two examples from outside of work?

Yes, they absolutely affect my life outside of work, especially at home. For example, I can't even sit through a movie with my son without constantly talking, checking my phone, or fiddling with my guitar. I also struggle with everyday personal tasks, like missing bill payments until I get a late notice or completely forgetting to call my divorce lawyer back.

Have these attention and restlessness symptoms caused clear problems in at least two areas of your life, such as work, home, school, relationships, finances, or driving? What are the main ways they’ve impaired you over time?

Yes, they've caused major issues at both work and home. At work, I've been written up for missing key details, my boss is questioning if I can handle this promotion, and I'm constantly staying late to fix my mistakes. This leaves me with almost no time to spend with my son or to keep up with my divorce paperwork.
